items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: one of the first movies I did was with Paul Butterfield and Nick Gravenites and Mike Bloomfield called “Steelyard Blues”... they wrote songs for the movie

ctx.x: Was that the first time that you had used a click track or are some records made that some of the pop records you’ve done, did you have a click track in your headphones?

Yeah it depends on the artists. Some people if they don’t, if they wrote the song with the drum machine pattern or some groove they came up with on a keyboard or something like that so we’d play along to that and maybe in the studio kind of pare it down to just the cowbell or just a click or sometimes they come in with a tempo in mind and sing it at that tempo but when recording starts you know they get excited or they lose that initial feel. So I’m always very careful to take a reading kind of when we run it…
conductor to make sure that it came out right. And then they underdubbed SMPTE and whatever else they needed to do the editing later.
